newsitem.title: USA: US Midcontinent premium eases on plentiful stocks.
newsitem.headline: US Midcontinent premium eases on plentiful stocks.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot premium unleaded gasoline differentials eased Monday on perceptions of plentiful stocks in the region as trade opened for the week, traders said.

Premium was talked 1.25 cents a gallon over regular unleaded for prompt deliveries in Chicago and Group Three, with later deliveries 1.50/1.75 cents over regular unleaded in the Midwest markets, traders said.
"Williams is chock full of premium," said one trader. Stepped-up production from Clark Refining and Marketing Co's Blue Island, Ill., refinery added to stocks in the region.
Unleaded gasoline and diesel fuel prices were heading lower early in the day on steady differentials and easing front-month NYMEX futures prices.
Chicago prompt unleaded gasoline opened the week unchanged at 4.50/5.00 cents over NYMEX December unleaded gasoline, with later barrels 3.75/4.25 cents a gallon over the print.
Chicago low sulphur diesel was bid 3.0 cents a gallon over NYMEX December heating oil for prompt deliveries and 2.50 cents over the screen for later deliveries, traders said.
Group Three unleaded was talked 5.50/5.75 cents a gallon over the print for prompt deliveries and 3.0/3.25 cents over for later deliveries, traders said.
Group Three prompt low sulphur diesel was talked 2.00/2.25 cents a gallon over the print, with later deliveries 1.00 cent weaker, traders said.

Prompt high sulphur diesel was bid 2.25 cents a gallon over the print in Chicago and 1.0 cent over in Group Three, where later deliveries eroded to 0.50 cent a gallon under the print on dormant agricultural demand.
